hero.title: Reading Objects
intro.0: A gentle step up from single-token drills. Write a few small objects that work together - one asks another for what it needs, one job lives in one place, and a class uses what is handed to it. No new theory - just the habits the SOLID drills will lean on.
task.1.title: Two objects talk
task.1.context: One object gets work done by [[concept:pr-collaboration|asking another and acting on the answer]]. Here a `Greeter` does not know the time itself - it asks a `Clock`, then picks a greeting. The pattern below asks a `Sensor`; do the same with the clock.
task.1.goal.0: Ask the `clock` for the hour, then return `"Good morning"` before 12, otherwise `"Good afternoon"`.
task.1.goal.1: This clock reads 9, so the output should be Good morning.
task.2.title: Ask another object for data
task.2.context:
A `Cart` should not store prices - that is the `PriceList`'s knowledge. The cart [[concept:pr-delegation|asks for a price]] and multiplies by the quantity. Keep the price list that is handed to the cart, then ask it.

The pattern below asks a `Catalog`; do the same with the price list.
task.2.goal.0: Store the `prices` handed into the constructor, then return the item's price times `qty`.
task.2.goal.1: A book is 10 and qty is 3, so the output should be 30.
task.3.title: A method that does one thing
task.3.context: A clear method has [[concept:pr-single-responsibility|a single, obvious result]] you can name. `Area` exists to do one calculation - the two sides multiplied - and nothing else. The pattern below is one job for a box; do the same for the rectangle.
task.3.goal.0: Return the area of the rectangle - `width` times `height`.
task.3.goal.1: For 4 by 5 the output should be 20.
task.4.title: Give each job its own class
task.4.context:
`Checkout` was doing two jobs at once: the maths (price times quantity) and the wording (turning that number into text). Two jobs in one method means two reasons to change one place.

Move the wording into `ReceiptFormatter`. `Checkout` keeps the maths and asks the formatter for the text. The pattern below splits a sale the same way.
task.4.goal.0: Give `ReceiptFormatter` a `Format(int total)` that returns `"Total: "` followed by the total.
task.4.goal.1: In `Pay`, build a formatter and ask it for the text. For 10 by 2 the output should be Total: 20.
task.5.title: Use what is handed in
task.5.context:
A class does not have to build its own tools. `Mailer` is given an `Outbox` through its constructor and uses that one - it never calls `new Outbox()` itself. A collaborator handed in from outside is easy to swap later.

The pattern below hands a `Printer` its `Ink`; do the same with the mailer and its outbox.
task.5.goal.0: Keep the `outbox` handed into the constructor, then send `"hello "` followed by `who` through it.
task.5.goal.1: For Sam the output should be sent: hello Sam.
task.6.title: Wire two objects and run
task.6.context:
Everything in one place now: a `Worker` is handed a `ConsoleLog` and reports through it. Keep the log, then have `Report` write the status through the log it was given. Two small objects collaborating is the shape of most real code.

The pattern below wires a `Bell` to a `Speaker`; do the same with the worker and its log.
task.6.goal.0: Keep the `log` handed into the constructor, then write the `status` through it in `Report`.
task.6.goal.1: `Main` reports work done, so the output should be work done.
task.7.title: Reading objects recap
task.7.summaryIntro: You read and wrote a few small objects working together. These are the habits the SOLID drills will lean on.
task.7.summaryItems.0.title: Objects collaborate -
task.7.summaryItems.0.text: one object asks another for what it needs, then acts on the answer.
task.7.summaryItems.1.title: One job per method -
task.7.summaryItems.1.text: a method that does exactly one thing is easy to name and trust.
task.7.summaryItems.2.title: Separate the jobs -
task.7.summaryItems.2.text: when a method does two things, give one of them its own class or method.
task.7.summaryItems.3.title: Receive, don't build -
task.7.summaryItems.3.text: let a class take its collaborator through the constructor, so it is easy to swap later.
task.7.summaryItems.4.title: Wire and run -
task.7.summaryItems.4.text: build the parts, hand them in, and let them talk - the shape of most real code.
task.7.summaryClose: Next you will meet these ideas by name in the design track: single responsibility, and depending on what is handed in.
